c.tagline: China's mild-weather 'Spring City' and the gateway to Yunnan and the Stone Forest.

taxi.fareNote: Cabs are metered with a flag-fall around ¥8; most locals hail or book through Didi, and paying via Alipay or WeChat is standard while foreign cards are rarely accepted.

emergency.note: 110 for police, 120 for ambulance/medical, and 119 for fire. English-speaking operators are limited, so carry your destination written in Chinese.

hood_landmark.Panlong District: Golden Horse and Jade Rooster Archways, Kunming
hood_landmark.Xishan & Dianchi Lake: Xishan Dragon Gate and Dianchi Lake, Kunming

avoid.reason: Keep an eye on bags around Kunming Railway Station and long-distance bus stations, known spots for petty theft and scam touts.

hood_desc: The walkable heart of the city around willow-lined Green Lake (Cuihu) Park and Yunnan University; leafy streets, cafes, a lively night market, and easy metro access make it the best base for first-timers.
Kunming's central-east downtown around the Golden Horse and Jade Rooster archways and the Nanping pedestrian street; dense with shopping malls, restaurants, and nightlife.
The scenic western district of forested hills rising above Dianchi Lake, home to Xishan Forest Park and the cliffside Dragon Gate; calm, green, and resort-like, good for nature and families.
A restored ancient town of temples, a Buddhist pagoda, and old snack streets in the city's southeast; suits travelers wanting local culture, authentic Yunnan eats, and cheaper stays.
A modern planned district southeast of the center with a university town, government offices, and the southern metro terminus; residential, quiet, and affordable but far from the sights.
lodging: Wyndham Grand Plaza Royale Colorful Yunnan Kunming

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; avoid tap water and ice made from it.

transit.hours: Metro trains run roughly 6:20 AM to 11:00 PM; city buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM, with limited night lines.
transit.note: The Kunming Metro (opened 2012) has six lines radiating from the center out to Chenggong and Changshui Airport; an extensive city bus network fills the gaps.
transit.pay: Pay by scanning a QR code in Alipay/WeChat or the Kunming Metro app, tap a rechargeable transit card, or use cash on buses (exact change). Fares start around ¥2.

bus: Intercity coaches to Dali, Lijiang, and other Yunnan cities
train: Kunming Railway Station and Kunming South Railway Station (high-speed rail to Guiyang, Guangzhou, and Shanghai; China-Laos Railway to Vientiane)

transit.m: Metro Line 6 to Tangzi, transfer to Line 3 for the city center (~50 min)
Airport express bus to the city center (~60 min)
Taxi to the city center (40-60 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected or customary in Kunming; restaurants and taxis do not add or anticipate a gratuity.

food.name: Crossing-the-bridge noodles
food.desc: Yunnan icon: a bowl of scalding chicken broth sealed under oil, into which you drop raw meat, quail egg and rice noodles at the table.

places.name: Jianxin Yuan
places.note: Century-old house with daily queues; the benchmark bowl in Kunming.

places.name: Huixiang Xilou
places.note: Ranked a must-visit restaurant, with lakeside views over Green Lake.

places.name: Qiaoxiangyuan
places.note: Long-established chain locals name alongside Jianxin Yuan for the classic set.

food.name: Steam pot chicken
food.desc: Qiguoji: chicken steamed in a purple-clay pot with a chimney, so the broth is condensed steam alone, often with medicinal herbs.

places.name: Lao Fangzi
places.note: Named by locals as the go-to for steam pot chicken.

places.name: Lao Dian Shanzhai
places.note: Dian cuisine with ethnic song and dance; roughly 70-100 CNY a head.

places.name: Xiaojipo No.8
places.note: Sit-down Dian restaurant regularly recommended for classic Yunnan dishes.

food.name: Wild mushroom hotpot
food.desc: Chicken broth simmered with boletus, matsutake and dozens of foraged fungi; a timer stops you eating before it is safely cooked.

places.name: Yi Ke Yin
places.note: Ranked first for broth quality; hidden alley setting near Green Lake Park.

places.name: Eight Kinds of Mushrooms Nanhua
places.note: Authentic Nanhua-sourced boletus, chicken mushroom and matsutake.

places.name: Guanxing Road hotpot street
places.note: Whole stretch of mushroom hotpot houses near the old airport and Expo Centre.

food.name: Rushan
food.desc: Bai-people rubbing cheese: stretched cows-milk sheets rolled on a stick, grilled over charcoal and brushed with rose jam or sugar.

places.name: Guandu Ancient Town snack lanes
places.note: Charcoal grills turning rushan sticks all afternoon among the temples.

places.name: Kunming Old Street
places.note: Restored old-town street lined with Yunnan snack stalls including rushan.

places.name: Nanqiang Street food alley
places.note: Central snack street where grilled cheese sits beside barbecue skewers.

food.name: Xuanwei ham dishes
food.desc: Yunnan's famous dry-cured mountain ham, sliced raw, steamed with honey or fried through rice and beans as a salty backbone.

places.name: Lao Dian Shanzhai
places.note: Menu built around Xuanwei ham; several dishes showcase it.

places.name: Xiaojipo No.8
places.note: Reliable Dian kitchen for ham, mushrooms and mountain vegetables.

places.name: Huixiang Xilou
places.note: Full Yunnan menu beyond the noodles, ham dishes included.

food.name: Shao erkuai
food.desc: Grilled pounded-rice flatbread folded around fried dough, pickles and chilli-sesame sauce - the Kunming breakfast in the hand.

places.name: Nanqiang Street food alley
places.note: Morning griddles turning erkuai for office workers.

places.name: Guandu Ancient Town snack lanes
places.note: Stalls make erkuai and doupi to order beside the pagodas.

places.name: Kunming Old Street
places.note: Easy central spot to try erkuai with other Yunnan street snacks.

food.name: Pu'er tea
food.desc: Yunnan's fermented dark tea, pressed into cakes and aged for years; served in small cups through repeated short infusions.

places.name: Cuihu Lake teahouses
places.note: Garden teahouses where locals play cards over pots of Pu'er.

places.name: Xiongda Tea Market
places.note: Wholesale tea market; most stalls will brew a tasting before you buy.

food.name: Yunnan coffee
food.desc: Arabica grown around Pu'er and Baoshan, now roasted locally; Kunming is the easiest place in China to drink single-origin Chinese coffee.

places.name: Wenlin Street cafes
places.note: Student cafe row roasting and pouring Yunnan single-origin beans.

places.name: Kunming Old Street cafes
places.note: Courtyard cafes in the restored quarter serving local-bean espresso.

landmarks: Stone Forest (Shilin)
A UNESCO-listed labyrinth of towering karst limestone pillars that looks like a petrified forest and is Yunnan's most photographed natural wonder.
Green Lake Park (Cuihu Park)
A lush lakeside park in the city center famous for its willow-lined causeways and the thousands of migratory red-billed gulls that winter there.
Yuantong Temple
Kunming's oldest and largest Buddhist temple, built around a central pond with an octagonal pavilion, offering a striking contrast of ancient architecture against the modern skyline.
Dragon Gate, Western Hills (Xishan)
A dramatic cliffside pathway and grotto carved into the mountainside overlooking Dianchi Lake, prized for its sweeping panoramic views.
Golden Temple (Jindian)
A rare all-bronze Taoist temple gleaming atop Mingfeng Mountain, one of the largest copper structures in China.
Dianchi Lake
Yunnan's largest lake, ringed by mountains and famous for its huge winter flocks of red-billed gulls and scenic waterfront promenades.
Yunnan Nationalities Village
An open-air cultural park recreating the traditional villages and architecture of Yunnan's 25 ethnic minorities, colorful and photogenic year-round.
Bamboo Temple (Qiongzhu Temple)
A hillside monastery renowned for its extraordinary collection of 500 vividly expressive clay arhat statues considered a masterpiece of Qing-dynasty sculpture.
Golden Horse and Jade Rooster Memorial Archway
A pair of ornate traditional Chinese archways marking the historic heart of downtown Kunming, illuminated beautifully at night.
Kunming World Horti-Expo Garden
A vast botanical park built for the 1999 World Horticultural Expo, featuring themed international gardens and greenhouses that make for vivid photography.

intl.op: China Railway Kunming Group / Laos-China Railway (LCR), trains D87/D88

train.note: The through Kunming-Vientiane service on the China-Laos railway began on 13 April 2023 and leaves from Kunming South, the high-speed station about 20 km southeast of the centre, calling at Luang Prabang before Vientiane. You must leave the train with all your luggage twice for passport control, once on the Chinese side and once at Boten in Laos, and there is no visa on arrival at that border - get a Laos e-visa in advance at https://laoevisa.gov.la/ before you travel. Chinese-leg tickets are sold on 12306 and Laos-leg tickets through the LCR operator at http://www.lcrc.ltd/ or its app, which is a genuine nuisance as the two fare systems do not talk to each other and the window opens only a few days out. Domestically, Kunming South has high-speed trains to Guangzhou (about 9 hours via Nanning), Shanghai (11.5-12 hours) and Beijing (about 12 hours), while Kunming Station keeps the overnight sleepers to Dali and Lijiang and the standard-gauge line south to Hekou on the Vietnamese border.

intl.op: international coaches from Kunming South Bus Station — counter sales; also resold via 12Go Asia at https://12go.asia/
international coaches from Kunming East Bus Station — counter sales; also resold via 12Go Asia at https://12go.asia/

bus.note: Kunming has four directional long-distance terminals - North, South, East and West - and international departures use the southern and eastern ones, both a fair way out on the metro or a taxi ride from the centre. The direct sleeper coach to Vientiane costs roughly US$80 (about 550,000 kip) and takes around 38 hours, which the new railway has made a much less attractive proposition. For Vietnam most travellers take a bus or the standard-gauge train to Hekou (about 7 hours), walk across the bridge to Lao Cai and pick up Vietnamese transport there; you need a Vietnamese visa or e-visa in hand as none is issued at the crossing. Tickets for international services are bought at the counter with your passport, and departures are checked against your visa before boarding.

ferry.note: Kunming is an inland plateau city roughly 700 km from the nearest coast, and although Dianchi Lake on its southern edge has sightseeing cruises there is no scheduled passenger ferry to anywhere.

half.name: Jiuxiang Cave
half.blurb: A cave system about 90 kilometers from Kunming with underground rivers, a waterfall, and a boat ride through chambers of stalactites and stalagmites.

full.name: Jianshui Ancient Town
full.blurb: A Qing-dynasty town roughly 220 kilometers south of Kunming with a swallow's-nest gorge, over a hundred temples, and dozens of stone bridges.

full.name: Dongchuan Red Land
full.blurb: Iron-rich farmland northeast of Kunming where crop fields turn deep red, orange, and yellow across terraced hillsides, best seen in dry-season light.
